I am 68 years old. I have worked these fields for 60 years. I never went to school. I cannot read books, but I can read soil and weather. My farm is 11.6 mu in Quzhou County. My household is two people, me and my wife. We have a well with a pump, and that is our water.

I never plan from nothing. I start from last year and change what failed. Last year my maize did 530 jin per mu. My cotton had worms because I only sprayed three times. My peanut was good. My mungbean was small because I did not irrigate enough. This year I fix those things.

For maize, I plant 4 mu in spring. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer, the yellow bag, 3 jin per mu. Before planting, I spread one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. That is the 15-15-15 kind. Then I rotary till. When the maize grows to my knee, I topdress with one 25-kilogram bag of urea per mu. The dealer says this is about 20 kilograms of nitrogen per mu. I also get about 7 kilograms of phosphorus and 6 kilograms of potassium from the base fertilizer. I irrigate three times: once after planting if it does not rain in three days, once when the stalks are growing fast in summer, and once when the ears are filling. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and insecticide once when I see corn borers. If my neighbors spray a second time for worms, I will spray twice. I expect 550 kilograms per mu this year.

For cotton, I plant 3 mu in spring. Cotton is money but it is back-breaking work. I use hybrid seed in the red bag. I put one 40-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu before rotary tilling. I topdress twice with urea: first at budding, 15 kilograms per mu, then at flowering, another 15 kilograms per mu. Total nitrogen is about 16 kilograms per mu. Phosphorus and potassium from the base are about 6 and 7 kilograms per mu. I irrigate three times: at budding, at peak flowering, and at boll opening. I spray four times this year. Last year three times was not enough. First spray for aphids, second and third for bollworms, fourth for mites. I expect 240 kilograms of seed cotton per mu.

For peanut, I plant 3 mu in spring. I use improved seed that I saved from last year, the big-pod kind. I put one 40-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and I also buy one extra 25-kilogram bag of potassium fertilizer for all 3 mu. That gives me about 7 kilograms of nitrogen, 6 kilograms of phosphorus, and 8 kilograms of potassium per mu. Peanut does not need much nitrogen because it makes its own, but it loves potassium. I rotary till. I irrigate twice: once at flowering and once at pod filling. I spray twice for leaf spot and pod borers. I expect 280 kilograms per mu.

For mungbean, I plant 1.6 mu in summer, after the spring crops are in the ground. I use my own traditional seed that I have kept for ten years. Mungbean is easy. I put one 25-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. That is about 3 kilograms nitrogen, 4 kilograms phosphorus, 3 kilograms potassium per mu. I irrigate twice. I spray twice for pod borers. I expect 90 kilograms per mu.

Why these amounts? Because this is what my neighbors do, and what I did last year. Old Wang across the road put 20 kilograms of nitrogen on his maize and got a good harvest. I will do the same. I would rather spend too much on fertilizer than too little. If I waste 50 yuan on extra fertilizer, I lose 50 yuan. If I lose yield, I lose hundreds of yuan and my family eats less. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting fertilizer is just a cost.

I think about my whole money. I do not hire labor because it is just me and my wife. We do the work ourselves. Maybe my nephew comes for two days to help pick cotton. I buy seed and fertilizer from the same dealer every year. He does not cheat me because I know the weight by hand. The well pump costs electricity, about 30 yuan each time I irrigate. I only irrigate when the leaves curl or the soil cracks.

That is my plan for this year.
